segments.text: Prediction time
In this case the decision is: Select contacts to call first. The moment of prediction decides which variables are allowed.
You state the moment in your own words; the agent restates it and records your answer. No data are read.
Every later step is judged against this moment.
Changing it later makes the availability decision, the policy, and the conclusion need confirmation again.
Feature availability
The case describes one row as: A customer contacted during a telephone campaign. For each variable you decide whether it is known at the prediction moment.
Each candidate variable gets one status. Uncertain variables are either excluded or included and listed as a limit.
Variables marked not available, or uncertain and excluded, never enter a model.

The intended use is: Teaching simulation: prioritize contacts when call capacity is limited. A policy turns scores into a number of actions the team can handle.
Each rule is evaluated on the stored validation predictions, with ties at the cut counted pro rata and paired bootstrap intervals.

The conclusion says what can be claimed, for which use, and with which limits.
You choose a verdict and write the text; keeping the baseline or calling the study inconclusive are valid results.
